Baal-perazim
BAY-uhl peh-RAY-zim
proper noun (place)
Hebrew Baal Peratsim, "lord of breakings-through"; where David defeated the Philistines as God broke forth like a flood.

📖 Biblical Definition

Baal-perazim was the place where King David, newly made king over all Israel, won his first great victory over the Philistines who had come up to seek him. David did not presume but inquired of the LORD, "Shall I go up to the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into mine hand?" and the LORD said, "Go up: for I will doubtless deliver the Philistines into thine hand" (2 Sam 5:19). David came and smote them, and said, "The LORD hath broken forth upon mine enemies before me, as the breach of waters. Therefore he called the name of that place Baalperazim" (2 Sam 5:20) — the place of breakings-through, for God had burst upon the enemy like a flood breaking through a dam. The prophet Isaiah later recalled this victory, saying the LORD would rise up "as in mount Perazim" to do His work (Isa 28:21). Baal-perazim stands in the dictionary as the place where God broke through like a flood, a witness to the blessing of inquiring of the LORD before battle, to the truth that victory comes from God who Himself breaks the power of the enemy, and to the readiness of God to burst forth in power for His people when they seek Him and obey.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Where David, having inquired of the LORD, defeated the Philistines; he named it Baal-perazim ("lord of breakings-through") because "the LORD hath broken forth upon mine enemies... as the breach of waters" (2 Sam 5:20).

BAAL-PERAZIM, proper noun. "Lord of breakings-through"; where David defeated the Philistines.

David's first great victory as king over all Israel.

Where he first inquired of the LORD before the battle (2 Sam 5:19).

Named for God breaking forth "as the breach of waters" (2 Sam 5:20).

Recalled by Isaiah as "mount Perazim" (Isa 28:21).

📖 Key Scripture

2 Sam 5:19 — "And David enquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go up to the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into mine hand? And the LORD said unto David, Go up: for I will doubtless deliver the Philistines into thine hand."

2 Sam 5:20 — "...And David said, The LORD hath broken forth upon mine enemies before me, as the breach of waters. Therefore he called the name of that place Baalperazim."

Isa 28:21 — "For the LORD shall rise up as in mount Perazim, he shall be wroth as in the valley of Gibeon..."

Psa 18:29 — "For by thee I have run through a troop; and by my God have I leaped over a wall."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Baal-perazim needs no defense from redefinition; its lessons are the blessing of seeking the LORD before acting, and the power of God who breaks through like a flood for His people.

expand to see more

Self-reliant action correction. The impulse of the flesh is to act first and seek God after. David, though a seasoned warrior and now king, inquired of the LORD before going up, and received both command and promise. The dictionary holds the wisdom of seeking God before battle: the believer is to acknowledge the LORD in all his ways, that He may direct his paths (Prov 3:6), and the victories that begin in prayerful inquiry of God are crowned with His blessing.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that God Himself breaks the power of the enemy. David did not boast that he had broken through, but that "the LORD hath broken forth upon mine enemies... as the breach of waters." The dictionary commends this confession: the victory belongs to God, who bursts upon the foe with irresistible power, and His people, running through troops and leaping walls, do so only by their God (Psa 18:29), to whom alone the praise is due.
